skill.name: privy
skill.description: Guides developers through Privy authentication, embedded wallet setup, policy controls, transaction workflows, and webhook verification.
skill.summary: Build secure Privy authentication and wallet integrations.

security_audit.summary: All 41 static detections are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code formatting, and documented Privy URLs. The skill is reference documentation and contains no executable automation, embedded secrets, prompt injection, or exfiltration intent. It emphasizes secure credential storage, policy testing, webhook verification, and transaction safeguards.

remediation.issue: Static analysis misclassifies Markdown backticks and documented endpoints as shell execution.
remediation.suggestion: Update scanner rules to distinguish Markdown code fences and inline endpoint paths from executable shell or Ruby syntax.

remediation.issue: Static analysis flags documented wallet transaction APIs as a cryptocurrency-wallet finding.
remediation.suggestion: Classify documented SDK method names separately from credentials, private keys, signed payloads, or transaction-execution code.

- **Webhook verification required:** Always verify webhook signatures before trusting the payload. U

- **Missing app client ID:** If deploying across multiple domains, configure app clients in the Dash

content.value_statement: Privy integrations combine authentication, wallet operations, and policy controls across several blockchains. This skill gives developers a structured setup path with safeguards for credentials, webhooks, and transactions.
actual_capabilities: Explains Privy client and server SDK entry points.
Guides authentication setup for email, social, passkey, and wallet login.
Describes embedded wallet creation and ownership models.
Maps wallet policies, signers, owners, and approval intents.
Covers transaction workflow requirements across supported chains.
Lists webhook verification, idempotency, and rate-limit safeguards.
limitations: Does not execute API calls, create wallets, or submit transactions.
Does not provide real App IDs, secrets, private keys, or credentials.
Does not replace Privy documentation or current API reference checks.
Does not determine legal, custody, or compliance requirements.

use_cases.title: Add login and embedded wallets
use_cases.description: Plan a consumer application flow for Privy login methods and wallet creation on first login.

use_cases.title: Secure backend wallet operations
use_cases.description: Design server-side wallet creation and transaction workflows with owners, signers, policies, and idempotency.

use_cases.title: Review production controls
use_cases.description: Check webhook verification, credential handling, policy coverage, chain identifiers, and transaction units before launch.

prompt_templates.title: Start a React integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add Privy authentication to a React application. List required dashboard settings and root provider configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Create embedded wallets
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to create an embedded Ethereum wallet on login and choose an appropriate ownership model.

prompt_templates.title: Define wallet policies
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Privy wallet policy requirements for a treasury workflow with approved recipients, amount limits, and multi-party approval.

prompt_templates.title: Review transaction readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Privy transaction architecture for credential storage, webhook verification, idempotency, rate limits, and policy gaps.

output_examples.input: What must I secure before using server-side Privy wallets?
output: Store App Secret only in server environment variables.
Assign explicit owners, signers, and wallet policies.
Use idempotency keys for wallet creation and transactions.
Verify webhook signatures before updating application state.

output_examples.input: How should I choose client-side or server-side wallets?
output_examples.output: Use client-side wallets when users control signing. Use server-side wallets for application-owned automation, with policies and approvals.

best_practices: Keep App Secrets and webhook signing secrets out of client code and logs.
Test deny-by-default policies before enabling production wallet actions.
Verify webhook signatures and use idempotency keys for critical operations.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode App Secrets or private keys in source files.
Do not trust webhook payloads before signature verification.
Do not submit transactions without checking chain IDs, units, policies, and approval state.

faq.question: Does this skill create a Privy account?
faq.answer: No. It explains setup steps but does not access dashboards or create accounts.

faq.question: Can this skill send blockchain transactions?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and does not execute transactions.

faq.question: Where should I store Privy credentials?
faq.answer: Store server credentials in protected environment variables or a managed secret store.

faq.question: Why are wallet policies important?
faq.answer: Policies constrain allowed actions, recipients, amounts, and approval requirements.

faq.question: Must I verify Privy webhooks?
faq.answer: Yes. Verify signatures before trusting webhook payloads or changing application state.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
